tone_statements.quote: [p.2] 先行研究では，スライアモン語のアクセントは非常に単純であると説明されてきた。すなわち，スライアモン語では強さアクセントが語の最初の母音（最初の音節）に置かれるというだけのものであった。... そして，アクセントに意味を担う弁別性があることが分かった。例えば，qʷúmut（ピッチは高低）は「（それを）口の中に入れる」という意味であるが，qʷúmùt（ピッチは高高）は「（それを）口の中に入れたままにする」という意味になる。形態的にはどちらも，qʷum という語根に，-ut という他動詞形成接尾辞が付いた形式で，アクセントのみが意味を弁別している。そして，強弱の差よりも，ピッチの高低の方が顕著に感じられる。... [p.3] スライアモン語では強さアクセントが語頭の母音に落ちる。そして，基本的にはそこから強弱の繰り返しでアクセントが付与される。... 状態アスペクトを表す形態素にはアクセントが落ちる
tone_statements.translation: [p.2] Previous research described Sliammon accent as very simple: stress accent is placed on the first vowel (first syllable) of the word, and nothing more. ... It then became clear that accent has a meaning-distinguishing function. For example, qʷúmut (pitch high-low) means 'put (it) in the mouth', whereas qʷúmùt (pitch high-high) means 'keep (it) in the mouth'. Morphologically both consist of the root qʷum plus the transitivizing suffix -ut; only the accent distinguishes the meanings. And the high/low pitch difference is perceived more saliently than the difference in intensity. ... [p.3] In Sliammon the stress accent falls on the word-initial vowel, and accent is basically assigned from there by alternation of strong and weak. ... Accent falls on the morpheme expressing stative aspect.

sources.citation: McCarthy, Mary & Tyler T. Schnoor. 2023. Yes/No Question Intonation in ʔayʔaǰuθəm. Papers for ICSNL 58, UBCWPL, pp. 333-339.
sources.quote: 'Primary word-level stress falls on the initial syllable in ʔayʔaǰuθəm. The assignment of secondary stress follows — with the exception of words containing certain suffixes — a left-aligned trochaic pattern in words that contain three or more syllables (Davis 1970; Watanabe 2003). Pitch is an important cue for stress (Watanabe 2003).'
sources.note: Recent summary of Watanabe 2003's stress description (initial primary, left-aligned trochaic secondary with suffix exceptions). downloaded now; confirms.

sources.citation: Menon, Aarya. 2023. A Phonetic Analysis of Stress Correlates and Stative Ambiguity in ʔayʔaǰuθəm. Papers for ICSNL 58, UBCWPL, pp. 340-347.
sources.quote: 'Primary stress in ʔayʔaǰuθəm occurs on the initial syllable, with the secondary stresses following a trochaic pattern (Blake 2000); secondary stress is assigned rightwards in alternating syllables ... some suffixes, such as the indirective (/-ʔəm/) appear to break this pattern by promoting themselves to take secondary stress (Watanabe 2003).' Instrumental result: duration (full vowels) / pitch (schwa) are the correlates of the initial primary stress; stative marked by raised pitch on the stressed vowel.
sources.note: Only instrumental study of word stress in the language; confirms initial primary stress and gives acoustic correlates. downloaded now.

sources.note: Research report devoted to Sliammon accent: earlier descriptions gave only word-initial stress, but accent is meaning-distinguishing, with pitch (high/low) more salient than intensity: qʷúmut (H-L) 'put it in the mouth' vs qʷúmùt (H-H) 'keep it in the mouth' (same root + transitivizer, only accent differs); initial stress with alternating rhythm confirmed by Praat, but the stative morpheme and the non-control transitivizer attract accent, sometimes as strong as the initial one (quoted). No accent-specific paper was published from the project (outputs are texts and a family chapter).

sources.note: Argues that raised pitch is contrastive and phonological in ʔayʔaǰuθəm: fixed initial primary stress plus a %H boundary tone on every word-initial syllable, and a floating H tone contributed by the stative morpheme (realised as high pitch on the second syllable, sometimes with no segmental exponent); privative H vs zero system; concludes the language is a pitch accent language in Hyman's (2006) sense, with both stress and tonal properties (quoted).
